editorial: Every time you think a town feels safe, secrets creep in like a burning ember. Salem's Lot (2024) subverts the classic vampire tale by turning the sleepy town of Jerusalem's Lot into a character of its own, whispering dread through cracked shutters and deserted streets. Joaquin Phoenix, as the quiet, haunted Ben Mears, carries every scene with almost no dialogue, letting his eyes and sparse gestures expose the horror lurking beneath the veneer of family reunion. The film’s pacing skims over the mounting terror, leaving the most chilling scenes to settle in instead of exploding, which can test your patience during the midsection. If you relish atmospheric dread over high octane gore, you'll find yourself cataloguing every shadow and subtle cue like a detective.
targetAudience: Ideal for horror aficionados who savor atmospheric dread and nuanced character work.
